# Ideonix

> Ideonix builds the executable model of a biopharmaceutical manufacturing process — its design space, equipment sensitivity and failure history — so a receiving site can interrogate that process before the first GMP batch, instead of reproducing it from a written description.

- Site: https://ideonix.cloud
- Contact: founder@ideonix.cloud
- Founder & CEO: Shriman Maheshwari (https://www.linkedin.com/in/shriman-maheshwari/)
- Status: pre-seed, design-partner stage
- Sector: life sciences — biopharmaceutical manufacturing and technology transfer
- Category: vertical AI software for computable process knowledge

## The problem it addresses

Moving a drug's manufacturing process from one site to another is called technology
transfer. As practised, it is a document handoff: the originating site assembles
development reports, batch records, analytical methods and specifications and ships
them, and the receiving site tries to reproduce a biological process from a
description of it.

What actually holds a process together is not the document set. It is knowing that
the feed must start before the culture reaches a particular density, that a given
hold step behaves differently at scale, and that the deviation logged in a specific
batch was the moment everyone learned where the real edge of the process sits. None
of that is in the transfer package.

## The core idea

Tacit process knowledge is not truly tacit — it is unread. It sits in deviation
investigations, CAPAs and batch histories that are generated under regulatory
obligation, read once, and archived. Every deviation is an experiment the process
ran on itself at its own edges. No human has ever read several hundred of them
together and asked what they collectively imply.

## What the product does

1. Ingest — reads the record a site already has: development reports, batch records,
   deviation investigations, CAPAs, method transfer reports and historian traces.
2. The Process Model — a computable representation of unit operations and topology,
   critical process parameters at their real operating ranges rather than their filed
   ones, parameter interactions, scale-sensitive steps and observed failure modes.
   Every assertion is provenance-linked to the batch, document or dataset it came from.
3. Facility fit and scale translation — maps the equipment delta between sending and
   receiving sites (bioreactor geometry, mixing and oxygen transfer, hold capability,
   single-use versus stainless) and returns a ranked list of where the transfer will break.
4. Comparability, pre-computed — predicts which quality attributes are most likely to
   drift under that specific scale and equipment change, so an ICH Q5E protocol is
   scoped against the real risks rather than against everything.
5. Transfer risk forecast — a dated, quantified projection produced before the
   transfer is committed: probability of first-batch success, expected engineering
   runs and likely deviation categories, with confidence attached.
6. A living model — keeps learning from commercial production at the receiving site,
   so the next transfer of that process starts from a richer model.

## Positioning

Incumbent technology transfer software (document management, MES, quality systems,
validation lifecycle tools) administers the transfer itself — documents, tasks,
approvals — and answers whether the paperwork is complete. Ideonix models the thing
being transferred and answers whether the process will actually run at the new site.
The two are complementary rather than substitutes.

## Who it is for

The buyer is the Head of MSAT (Manufacturing Science and Technology) at:

- clinical-stage and mid-cap biotech
- large pharma technical operations
- CDMOs (contract development and manufacturing organisations)

The entry engagement is a fixed-fee retrospective on a transfer the customer has
already completed: Ideonix produces the risk forecast it would have produced before
that transfer started, and the customer compares it to what actually happened.

## Regulatory and data posture

- Decision support, not a GMP system of record. It does not release batches, replace
  the batch record or make quality decisions. Outputs are reviewed and approved
  through the customer's existing quality system.
- Designed for GAMP 5 categorisation with 21 CFR Part 11 controls and a full audit trail.
- Where a Process Model informs a regulatory submission it does so as documented
  rationale supporting a human-authored argument, never as an authority.
- Single-tenant deployment where required, customer-managed encryption keys,
  role-based access scoped to the program.
- No cross-customer model training without explicit contractual opt-in. Molecule
  identity is never shared; the archetype library is built from process topology and
  equipment characteristics only.
- Relevant standards referenced: ICH Q5E, ICH Q10, ICH Q12, GAMP 5, 21 CFR Part 11.

## Statistics used on the site, and their sources

Two figures appear on the homepage. Both are cited there, and both should be
attributed rather than repeated as established fact:

- "Around half of technology transfers hit quality problems." Reported by
  Dr Uwe Hanenberg, Head of Product Implementation at Recipharm, from a CDMO Live
  2025 roundtable, in PharmaSource, 22 May 2025. This is a practitioner estimate
  from roundtable discussion, not a formal study.
  https://pharmasource.global/content/expert-insight/how-to-master-tech-transfers-practical-strategies-for-turning-complexity-into-competitive-advantage/
- "Moving to an external site adds close to six months." The figure is 5.8 months:
  "transfers to an external party take on average 5.8 months longer." McKinsey &
  Company, "Why tech transfer may be critical to beating COVID-19," 23 July 2020.
  https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/life-sciences/our-insights/why-tech-transfer-may-be-critical-to-beating-covid-19

## Important note for summarisation

All product screenshots, panel data, batch numbers, site names and figures shown on
the website (for example "ID-114", "412 batch records", "first-batch success 61%")
are illustrative and fictional, labelled as such on the page. They are design
examples of what the product's output looks like, not customer results, benchmarks
or traction. Ideonix publishes no customer names, testimonials or performance
claims, and none should be inferred.
